questions.question: To diagnose an adrenal adenoma on a dedicated adrenal CT, what is the standard threshold for "Absolute Washout" at 15 minutes?
questions.detail: An absolute enhancement washout of 60% or greater is highly specific for a benign adenoma.

questions.question: If a non-contrast CT phase is not available, a "Relative Washout" can be calculated. What is the threshold for a benign adenoma?
questions.detail: A relative washout of greater than 40% is used when only the venous and delayed phases are available.

questions.question: Which finding on CT is pathognomonic for an adrenal myelolipoma?
questions.detail: Myelolipomas are benign tumors composed of fat and hematopoietic elements; identifying fat on CT is diagnostic.

questions.question: Adrenal "Pheochromocytomas" are often called "10% tumors." Which of the following is NOT part of the classic 10% rule?
questions.detail: Hypertension is a very common presenting symptom, far exceeding 10% of cases. The classic rule includes 10% malignant, bilateral, extra-adrenal, and familial.

questions.question: In a neonate with a suprarenal mass, identifying which of the following features on serial ultrasound is most indicative of an "Adrenal Hemorrhage" rather than neuroblastoma?
choices: C. Progressive decrease in size and involution
questions.detail: Neonatal adrenal hemorrhage characteristically resolves or calcifies over weeks, whereas neuroblastoma will continue to grow.

questions.question: What is a "Collision Tumor" in the context of adrenal imaging?
choices: A. Two separate tumors (e.g., an adenoma and a metastasis) occurring in the same gland
B. A tumor that invades the kidney
C. A tumor caused by trauma
D. A Pheochromocytoma that secretes two different hormones
E. A tumor that crosses the midline
questions.detail: This refers to the coincidence of two distinct pathologies within the same adrenal gland.

questions.question: Which syndrome is characterized by primary hyperaldosteronism, often due to a functioning adrenal adenoma?
questions.detail: Conn syndrome involves the overproduction of aldosterone, typically presenting with hypertension and hypokalemia.

questions.question: Adrenal cortical carcinoma (ACC) is typically distinguished from an adenoma on imaging by which feature?
choices: B. Presence of microscopic fat only
C. Large size (> 4-6 cm), irregular margins, and central necrosis
questions.detail: ACCs are usually large, aggressive, and heterogeneous (due to necrosis) at the time of diagnosis.

questions.question: Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome involves hemorrhagic destruction of the adrenal glands, classically associated with which infection?
questions.detail: This syndrome is a life-threatening adrenal crisis resulting from fulminant septicemia, classically with Neisseria meningitidis.

questions.question: Which nuclear medicine tracer is the "gold standard" for localizing a pheochromocytoma?
questions.detail: I-123 MIBG is a norepinephrine analog taken up by chromaffin tissues, making it the standard for localizing these tumors.
